---
applyTo: "app/actions/**/*.rb,spec/actions/**/*.rb"
---

# Actions

- Write an action for one task that could be run from more than one place, e.g. a form, a job, the console or a rake task, and put it in `app/actions/`, e.g. `Posts::ArchivePost` in `app/actions/posts/archive_post.rb`.
- Keep actions separate from command forms. A command form handles what the user submits and returns the resource or `false`, e.g. `PublishPostForm`. An action is its own object that does a task, e.g. `Posts::ArchivePost`.
- Keep calls from one action to another rare. Call another action only when it is part of the same task, and no caller would want one without the other.
- When the work needs more than one step, run the steps from a job, not from an action. Enqueue a job for a later step that can wait, e.g. `Posts::PublishPost.call(post, publisher: post.scheduled_by)` then `NotifySubscribersJob.perform_later(post)` in `PublishScheduledPostJob`. Keep `Posts::PublishPost` to publishing the post.
- An action may enqueue a job, e.g. `NotifySubscribersJob.perform_later(post)`. When it enqueues inside a transaction, make sure the job waits for the commit, e.g. with `self.enqueue_after_transaction_commit = true` in the job class.
- When enqueuing a job takes more than a plain `perform_later`, e.g. working out when the job should run and what it should run with, put it in an action whose name starts with `Enqueue`, e.g. `Posts::EnqueuePublish` calls `PublishScheduledPostJob.set(wait_until: post.publish_at).perform_later(post)`. For a plain `perform_later`, enqueue the job in the caller.
- When an action calls another action, rescue the other action's error and raise your own, e.g. `rescue ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid, Posts::UnpublishPost::Error => e` then `raise Error, e.message` in `Posts::ArchivePost`. Never let another action's error escape your action.
- Raise the error for the same cause, e.g. `rescue Posts::SendNewsletter::ServiceError => e` then `raise ServiceError, e.message`, not `raise Error`. Put that `rescue` before the one for the other action's `Error`.
- If an action should carry on when another action it calls fails, don't call that action from it. Run it as a separate step from a job.
- Put each action in a module named after the resource it works on, in the plural, e.g. `Posts`. Name the action after the task, starting with a verb. The name can include the resource, e.g. `Posts::ArchivePost`, not `ArchivePost` or `Posts::ArchivePostAction`.
- Inherit every action from `ApplicationAction` in `app/actions/application_action.rb`, whose class method `call` runs `new(...).call` and returns `nil`. Give each action an `initialize` that keeps its arguments in private `attr_reader`s, and an instance method `call` that does the task.
- Write the parts of an action in this order, without comment headings: error classes, `include` lines, validations, `initialize`, `call`, then `private` with the `attr_reader`s followed by any private methods, e.g. `class Error < StandardError; end`, `include ValidatedCallable`, `validates :post, :publisher, ...`, `def initialize(post, publisher:)`, `def call` and `attr_reader :post, :publisher` in `Posts::PublishPost`.
- Call an action with the class method, e.g. `Posts::ArchivePost.call(post)`, not `Posts::ArchivePost.new(post).call`.
- Pass an action the records it works on, never their IDs, e.g. `Posts::ArchivePost.call(post)`, not `Posts::ArchivePost.call(post.id)`. Find the records in the caller, e.g. a controller loads the post. Never look a record up by ID inside an action.
- Make the resource an action works on its first positional argument, and pass every other argument as a keyword, e.g. `Posts::PublishPost.call(post, publisher: current_user)` with `def initialize(post, publisher:)`.
- Never pass a record with unsaved changes to an action, e.g. `post.title = title` then `Posts::PublishPost.call(post, publisher: current_user)`. Save the changes first, or pass the new values as keywords and set them in the action, e.g. `Posts::PublishPost.call(post, publisher: current_user, title:)`.
- When an action works on many records, pass the records and name the action in the plural, e.g. `Posts::ArchivePosts.call(author.posts)`. Never pass their IDs. Work on every record given, and leave picking the records to the caller.
- Pass either a relation (or association) or an array of records to an action on many records, and pick one for each action. Pass the same kind from every caller, and never let the action accept both, e.g. by checking `posts.is_a?(Array)`. Prefer a relation when there could be many records.
- In an action on many records, write them in one statement when the task can be done in SQL and no callback, validation or `dependent:` on the model must run for the change, e.g. `posts.update_all(archived_at: now, updated_at: now)` with `now = Time.zone.now`, inside a transaction when it writes more than once. Update the relation's own records last, because each statement runs the relation's query again, e.g. `Comment.where(post: posts).update_all(locked: true, updated_at: now)` before `posts.update_all(archived_at: now, updated_at: now)`.
- Always pass `updated_at` to `update_all`, e.g. `update_all(locked: true, updated_at: Time.zone.now)`, because `update_all` doesn't set it.
- When each record needs the model's validations, callbacks or a lock, load them with `find_each`, or loop with `each` over an array, and call the single-record action for each, e.g. `posts.find_each { |post| Posts::ArchivePost.call(post) }`. Avoid wrapping that loop in a transaction.
- Prefer `find_each` to `each` when you loop over a relation, e.g. `posts.find_each`, not `posts.each`.
- Never authorise the user or validate user input in an action. Do both in the caller before it calls the action, e.g. `authorize @post` in the controller and validations in the form. Trust the caller, and do the task.
- To check an action's arguments, include `ValidatedCallable` from `app/actions/concerns/validated_callable.rb`, which adds `ActiveModel::Validations` and runs `validate!` before `call`, then validate them, e.g. `validates :post, :publisher, presence: true, unmodified: { allow_blank: true }` in `Posts::PublishPost`.
- Never use an action's argument validations to control the app's flow. Never rescue `ActiveModel::ValidationError` from an action, and never raise it again as the action's `Error`.
- Never return a value from an action, and never use the value an action returns.
- When a caller needs a value from an action's work, have the action save it on a record the caller holds, and read it from the record after the call, e.g. `@post.newsletter_id` after `Posts::SendNewsletter.call(@post)`.
- When another service accepts an ID from you, generate the ID in the caller and pass it to the action, e.g. `newsletter_id = SecureRandom.uuid` then `Posts::SendNewsletter.call(@post, newsletter_id:)`.
- When an API client tracks a request to another service, create a record for the request first with your own ID, e.g. `has_secure_token :reference` on `NewsletterDelivery`. Send your ID to the service, and give the client your ID, never the service's.
- Never pass a value back from an action through a block or a result object, e.g. `Posts::SendNewsletter.call(post) { |newsletter_id| ... }` or `Result.new(success: true, value: response.id)`.
- For more ways to get a value from an action's work, see https://bmorrall.github.io/happy_rails/patterns/values-from-actions/.
- When an action's task fails, raise an error, e.g. with `update!`, rather than returning `false`.
- Let an error that no caller should handle pass through the action unchanged.
- When a caller is meant to handle an error, define a custom `Error` class inside the action that inherits from `StandardError`, e.g. `class Error < StandardError; end` in `Posts::ArchivePost`. In `call`, rescue the errors the caller should handle and raise them again as the action's `Error`, e.g. `rescue ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid => e` then `raise Error, e.message`.
- When an action can fail for more than one cause and callers handle the causes differently, give each cause its own error class that inherits from the action's `Error`, e.g. `class RejectedError < Error; end` and `class ServiceError < Error; end` in `Posts::SendNewsletter`. Callers rescue the class for the cause they handle, or `Error` for them all.
- When another service fails, e.g. it returns a 500 or times out, raise a `ServiceError` for it from the client's base error class, after the `rescue` for causes the user can fix, e.g. `rescue NewsletterClient::UnprocessableError` then `rescue NewsletterClient::Error => e` and `raise ServiceError, e.message`.
- When an action writes more than once, wrap the writes in `ActiveRecord::Base.transaction` inside the action, e.g. `post.update!(archived_at: Time.zone.now)` and `post.comments.update_all(locked: true, updated_at: Time.zone.now)` in `Posts::ArchivePost`. Don't open a transaction in an action that writes once.
- When an action relies on a lock, take it inside the action with `with_lock`, e.g. `post.with_lock do ... end` in `Posts::PublishPost`. Never take the lock in the caller.
- When an action that locks a record needs new values, set them inside the `with_lock` block, never before it.
- You may check a condition before taking a lock, to skip the lock when the work is not needed, e.g. `return if post.published?`. Always check it again inside the lock, e.g. `next if post.published?` as the first line of the `with_lock` block.
- Use `next` to leave a `transaction` or `with_lock` block early. Never use `return` inside the block.
- When a check before or inside a lock fails, do nothing if the work is already done, e.g. the post is already published. Raise the action's `Error` when the caller needs to know, e.g. to show a form error. Do the same in both checks.
- When an action locks more than one record, lock them in the same order every time, the parent before its children, e.g. the post before its comments.
- Never call another service inside a transaction, e.g. `NewsletterClient.new.create_newsletter(post)`. Call it first, then save its reply in the transaction, e.g. `post.update!(newsletter_id: response.id)`.
- When an action does not need another service's reply, never call the service from the action. Enqueue a job that calls it instead, e.g. `NotifySubscribersJob.perform_later(post)`, with `self.enqueue_after_transaction_commit = true` in the job class.
- When an action needs another service's reply, include `NonTransactionalCallable` from `app/actions/concerns/non_transactional_callable.rb`, which raises in the class method `call` when `ActiveRecord::Base.connection.current_transaction.joinable?` and otherwise calls `super`, e.g. `include NonTransactionalCallable` in `Posts::SendNewsletter`. Never call such an action inside a transaction.
- Run work that must wait for the commit and is not a job, e.g. a Turbo broadcast, in an `ActiveRecord.after_all_transactions_commit` block, e.g. `ActiveRecord.after_all_transactions_commit { post.broadcast_refresh }`. Never rely on running it after the action's own transaction block.
- Never raise `ActiveRecord::Rollback` in an action. Raise a real error, so the whole transaction rolls back.
- Rescue errors to raise them again as the action's `Error` outside the transaction block, e.g. with a `rescue` on `call`, including another action's errors. Never rescue an error inside a `transaction` or `with_lock` block and carry on.
- Start the name of an action whose write must stay saved when other work fails with `Record`, e.g. `Posts::RecordLinkCheck` saves `link_check_status` on the post.
- Never call a `Record` action inside a transaction, including a nested `requires_new: true` block. Call it before or after the transaction block, e.g. `Posts::RecordLinkCheck.call(post)` before `ActiveRecord::Base.transaction do`. Read its result from the record, e.g. `return false if post.link_check_failed?`.
- Write action specs as unit specs. Stub and mock the models and other objects the action uses, and check that the action calls them with the right arguments, e.g. `post = instance_double(Post)` then `expect(post).to receive(:update!).with(archived_at: an_instance_of(ActiveSupport::TimeWithZone))` before `described_class.call(post)`.
- In action specs, name the `describe` block after the method the spec calls, e.g. `describe ".call"`.
- If an action spec needs a lot of stubs to set up, split the action into smaller actions. If the action is simple but its objects take a lot of stubbing, e.g. a chain of associations, build real records with `create` instead, e.g. `create(:post)`, not `build_stubbed`.
- In action specs, check the action's `Error` by stubbing a collaborator to raise the original error, e.g. `allow(post).to receive(:update!).and_raise(ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid)` then `expect { described_class.call(post) }.to raise_error(described_class::Error)`.
